title: Mastery
summary: Points earned by good goes, never taken away, up to mastery, with a ledger of every change.
description: Mastery says a lesson is known for good. It is earned by practising well, never by waiting, and only ever grows; passes further apart are better evidence.

stories.want: to master a lesson by practising, without waiting for check-ins
stories.soThat: a deadline two days away is still reachable

stories.as: a learner looking at a lesson's points
stories.want: to see every change and why
stories.soThat: the score is something I can trust

requirements.text: The first pass of a lesson earns `mastery.first-pass` mastery points.
A later pass on the same day as the last go earns `mastery.same-day`.
A later pass a day or more after the last go earns 15, plus up to 20 more as the gap grows to 14 days.
An ace earns a quarter more than a pass would.

A go short of a pass earns a share of what a pass would in the same situation: a drill none at or below `mastery.credit-from` of its score right and all of it at `drill.pass-share`, rising linearly between and rounded down; a conversation half for a partial and none for a fail. It does not mark the lesson passed.

history.text: A partial earns half of what a repeat pass would at the same gap, rounded down, and does not mark the lesson passed.
history.reason: Credit jumped at the pass and partial cut-offs, so one answer could halve a go's points; credit in proportion to the score rewards every right answer without a cliff.

requirements.text: No go takes mastery points away, a fail included.

history.text: A fail costs `mastery.fail-cost` points; a fail on extra practice costs none.
history.reason: A fail took points for the moment of learning and discouraged the learner; the schedule already answers a fail by bringing the lesson back tomorrow.

requirements.text: Points stay between 0 and `mastery.full`, and stop at `mastery.held-at` until the lesson has been passed on two different days.

A lesson is mastered when it has been passed and has `mastery.full` points; once mastered it is never due again and nothing takes mastery or points away. Its words can still come back as a light review in today's lessons.
A writing lesson is mastered only when it has also been passed without help.

deprecation.reason: It said what CONV-10 says; the rule is kept once, with writing lessons.

requirements.text: Every graded go writes a row in the lesson's mastery ledger, with the points before and after and the reason, including a go that changed nothing; the go that masters the lesson adds a second row marking it mastered.
Ledger rows are never changed after they are written.
The ledger is shown on the lesson's page as Mastery points and is readable by the tutor.
A lesson's points from before the ledger existed are shown as one starting line; nothing is backfilled.

values.description: The points at which a lesson is mastered.
Where points stop until a lesson has passes on two days.
What a later pass on the same day earns.
The share of a drill right at or below which it earns no mastery points.

deprecation.reason: Mastery points only grow: a fail earns what its score earns and costs nothing.
